name: Waldenström macroglobulinemia
aliases: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma with IgM monoclonal gammopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus criteria for diagnosis of Waldenström macroglobulinemia

criteria.description: Presence of lymphoplasmacytic infiltration in bone marrow
Detection of monoclonal IgM protein in serum
Presence of symptoms or signs attributable to WM such as hyperviscosity syndrome or anemia
Exclusion of other B-cell lymphoproliferative disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Bone marrow lymphoplasmacytic infiltration plus monoclonal IgM in serum with clinical features consistent with WM and exclusion of other lymphomas
diagnosticCriteria.notes: MYD88 L265P mutation testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory

searchTerms: bone marrow filled with abnormal lymphoplasmacytic cells

bone marrow involvement by lymphoplasmacytic cells

pathognomonic.notes: May cause visual disturbances, headache, and bleeding

common.notes: Due to platelet dysfunction or hyperviscosity

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment due to monoclonal IgM deposition
searchTerms: kidney problems from IgM deposits

laboratory: Serum protein electrophoresis showing monoclonal IgM spike
Bone marrow biopsy with lymphoplasmacytic infiltration
Presence of MYD88 L265P mutation in majority of cases
imaging: CT scan showing lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly
MRI brain in suspected Bing-Neel syndrome
genetic: MYD88 L265P mutation detected in >90% of cases
CXCR4 mutations in subset of patients

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant IgG or IgA paraprotein rather than IgM
Higher plasma cell percentage in marrow

redFlags: Rapidly progressive hyperviscosity symptoms (blurred vision, headache, confusion)
Severe anemia with symptomatic fatigue or dyspnea
Neurological deficits suggestive of CNS involvement (Bing-Neel syndrome)
